director.label: Director
director.heading: A word from the director
body: Welcome to the official page of the Electronic Computer Department at the University of Warith Al-Anbiyaa — the department responsible for building, running and sustaining the university's digital infrastructure.

Over the past years we have made real progress in extending the network, automating academic and administrative work, protecting our data and developing our staff. A great deal remains ahead of us, and we pursue it in partnership with every college and department.
I invite the university's staff and students to reach out to us on anything concerning our services. Your feedback is the foundation we build our work on.
director.name: Eng. Abbas Nouri
director.imageAlt: Eng. Abbas Nouri, Director of the Electronic Computer Department

overview.label: About the department
heading: Vision, mission
and objectives

pillars.title: Vision
pillars.body: To be the trusted technical reference inside the university, with its academic and administrative services delivered on a secure, stable digital infrastructure that meets recognised higher-education standards.

pillars.title: Mission
pillars.body: To provide an IT infrastructure that serves teaching, research and administration; to build and protect the university's electronic systems and data; and to grow the digital capability of its staff and students.

objectives: Operate the campus network and internet service and keep them available throughout the academic year.
Automate academic and administrative procedures and reduce reliance on paper processes.
Build and maintain the university's systems and databases, and consolidate its sources of data.
Protect data and systems in line with the university's approved information-security policies.
Provide technical support and hardware maintenance to colleges and departments within defined response times.
Train staff and students through courses and workshops in networking, databases and information security.

items.title: Information Security Workshop
items.imageAlt: A training lecture in the teaching hall
items.excerpt: A two-day workshop introducing staff to the university's data-protection policy and to handling accounts and university mail safely.
outline: Recognising phishing messages and suspicious links
What to do when a security incident is suspected
body: The workshop aims to raise security awareness among university staff, who are the first line of defence for student data and academic records.
It pairs the policy material with hands-on exercises against real phishing messages received by university mail, walking through the checks to make before opening any link or attachment.
Register through the administrative unit in your college or by writing to the department. Places are limited by the capacity of the training hall.

items.title: Network Administration Course
items.imageAlt: A training workshop in a university hall
items.excerpt: A hands-on course in network fundamentals, device configuration and fault handling, for technical staff across the colleges.
outline: Configuring switches and wireless access points
body: The course gives a practical grounding to whoever looks after the network inside their college, so common faults can be diagnosed and cleared without waiting on the department's team.
Exercises run on real hardware in the computer lab and cover configuring switches and access points and reading device logs.
Participants are expected to be comfortable with operating systems and desktop network settings before attending.

items.title: Electronic Examination System Course
items.excerpt: A course introducing teaching staff to building, running and reporting on electronic examinations on the university platform.
outline: Building and categorising the question bank
Setting up an exam, its timing and attempts
Invigilating and handling issues during the exam
body: The course covers the full life of an electronic exam, from building the question bank through to producing and reading the results.
A complete mock exam runs during the session, with participants taking the instructor and student roles in turn so they see both interfaces.
It is held ahead of the monthly examination period and is recommended for anyone using the platform for the first time.

items.question: How do I get a university email account?
items.answer: Apply through the administrative unit in your college. The center creates the account within two working days and sends the credentials back to that unit.

items.question: How do I report a technical fault?
items.answer: Through the center's help desk or by writing to the official address, stating your college, the device number and a description of the fault.

items.question: How do I connect to the campus wireless network?
items.answer: Use your existing university account after selecting the university network from the list available inside the campus.

items.question: Does the center run training courses?
items.answer: Yes. The center runs courses in networking, databases and information security for university staff and students.

items.question: What are the center's working hours?
items.answer: Sunday to Thursday, 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM, excluding official holidays.

cta.heading: Need technical support from the center?
cta.body: Our team is ready to receive your request and follow it through to resolution.

items.author: Network & Communications
items.title: Center completes the campus wireless network expansion
items.imageAlt: A computer lab at the University of Warith Al-Anbiyaa
items.excerpt: The final phase of the wireless expansion is complete, covering the colleges, teaching halls and student facilities across the campus.
body: The Network & Communications division has completed the final phase of the campus wireless expansion, covering the colleges, the teaching halls and the student facilities.

The work included installing additional access points, upgrading the distribution hardware and re-planning channel allocation to cut interference, alongside separating the guest network from the staff network for security.
Staff and students can join the network with their existing university account, with no separate password per location.
The division monitors network performance daily and takes user reports through the department's help desk.

items.author: Systems & Databases
items.title: Updated release of the digital services portal goes live
items.imageAlt: A student using the university digital services
items.excerpt: A new release brings student and staff services into a single interface, with faster responses and a mobile-ready layout.
body: The Systems & Databases division has released an updated version of the digital services portal, bringing student and staff services into a single interface.
The new release improves response times, adds a layout that works on phones, and gives each user a record for tracking the status of their requests.
Data sources have also been consolidated with the academic systems, reducing duplicate data entry and the errors that come with it.
Further services will be added to the portal next term in coordination with the colleges and departments.

items.author: Training & Development
items.title: Information security course concludes for college staff
items.imageAlt: A participant in a training course at the department
items.excerpt: A three-day course covering data-protection policy, password management and recognising phishing messages.
body: The Training & Development division has concluded its information security course for college staff, held over three days in the department's training hall.
The course covered data-protection policy, password management, recognising phishing messages, and the steps to follow when a security incident is suspected.
Staff from the administrative units across the colleges took part, and certificates of attendance were issued at the close.
The division plans further courses of the same kind through the academic year, alongside courses in networking and databases.
